title: Language-model loss and comparison
description: Keep target accounting, held-out evidence and initialization variation distinct when comparing the same text model.

terms.definition: An observed token selected by the loss mask. This fixture scores content and end-of-sequence targets, excludes padding, and uses beginning-of-sequence only as context.
The negative natural logarithm of the probability assigned to an observed target. Add target losses before dividing by their total count; the resulting mean is measured in nats per target.

The exponential of mean negative log-likelihood, computed after target-weighted aggregation. Lower values mean higher likelihood for the selected targets under a comparable scoring setup; they do not identify every learned linguistic property.
Loss measured on the documents used for optimizer updates. Its decline shows a better fit to those selected targets, which can occur while validation loss worsens.
Loss measured on documents excluded from optimizer updates and baseline fitting. This chapter inspects the same validation split repeatedly, so it is not an untouched final test.
In this bounded experiment, training loss decreases while validation loss increases between evaluated checkpoints. A gap between the two losses alone does not establish that time-dependent pattern.

The existing count model assigns a next-token probability using only the previous token and add-one smoothing. It is fitted only to training documents and scores the same target occurrences as the neural model.

Differences across the three fixed model-initialization seeds while the split and training policy remain fixed. Their mean, sample standard deviation and observed range are descriptive; they are not a population confidence interval.
